topics.label: Introduction to complement lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing, setting expectations and introducing the lecture topic.

topics.label: Complement system overview, naming conventions, and central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the foundational concepts of complement, its nomenclature conventions, and the central role of C3 cleavage.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation and trigger threshold
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three pathways of complement activation—alternative, lectin, and classical—and how convertases build toward a local trigger threshold.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of activated complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the downstream immune effector functions triggered by complement activation, including opsonization, inflammation, and target cell lysis.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins and mechanisms that protect healthy host cells from inadvertent complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the distinct clinical presentations, infection risks, and autoimmune manifestations resulting from specific complement deficiencies.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion mechanisms and biotechnological applications
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how microbial pathogens evade complement defenses and how bacterial evasion factors are leveraged in medical and laboratory settings.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing framing, thanking students and previewing the upcoming lecture on the adaptive immune system.
